newsitem.title: USA: Karnal bunt found in 1 Tennessee county - official.
newsitem.headline: Karnal bunt found in 1 Tennessee county - official.

text.p: Karnal bunt fungus was found in winter wheat grown in one Tennessee county and is suspected in six other counties as well, said Tom Womack, spokesman for the Tennessee Department of Agriculture.

"We've had one confirmed positive test by USDA for karnal bunt in Tennessee," Womack said. "We have as many as six other counties in Tennessee where there is a suspect positive of karnal bunt but not confirmed."
Womack said USDA discovered the fungus in soft red winter wheat grown in Giles County in south-central Tennessee. About 95 percent of the wheat grown in the state is of that variety, he said.
He said the U.S. Agriculture Department was not sure how much wheat was affected but added, "we expect USDA will, in the next couple of days set up further testing."
The contaminated wheat was found in both on-farm and commercial storage bins, Womack said.

USDA has been testing for karnal bunt across the country since it was discovered in March in Arizona. The fungus, named after a town in India where it was first discovered, has also been found in New Mexico, Texas, California and Alabama.
